record.title: Radxa ZERO 3W as a bare host: 40-pin header + 22-pin MIPI CSI, no port standard; every pin identifier is the design file's assertion
record.provides_basis: A bare host: pin identifiers come from the DESIGN FILE through .wire() and .declare_segment(), recorded as the user's assertion — the esp32s3_raw arrangement. The header_40pin and buses_the_microduck_uses blocks below are the vendor's pin→function table those identifiers are checked against by a reader, not by this loader.
record.adjacency_rule_basis: There is no connector standard on the 40-pin header, so there is no adjacency question. Stated, not absent.

record.host_note: The Microduck's compute board (device tree compatible 'radxa,zero-3w', 'rockchip,rk3566' — research/raw/deploy_audio_i2c3-pihat.dts:46; docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §2). Four vendor documents were fetched into docs/fetched/ on 2026-09-02 and every figure below names which one: [brief] = Radxa ZERO 3W Product Brief RAD-DOC-0084 Revision 1.10 2026-06-26 (9 pp); [sch1.12] = schematic 'Zero 3W' REV V1.12, dated 'Monday, November 25, 2024', 22 sheets; [sch1.11] = schematic V1.11, 2023-09-21, 22 sheets; [wiki] = docs.radxa.com/en/zero/zero3/hardware-design/hardware-interface (HTML, CC BY 4.0 per its footer); [product] = radxa.com/products/zeros/zero3w/ (HTML).

record.identity_vs_fitted: Pollen's SKU (RAM/eMMC/header) and board revision: CANNOT DETERMINE. Press kit says 1 GB / 32 GB — the brief's SKU table p.8 has NO 1 GB + 32 GB row ('1GB' pairs with 'N/A' or '8GB' eMMC: RS107‑D1E0H1W15 / D1E8H1W15). Either the press kit's storage figure, or the SKU table, or a custom build — a production teardown settles it. The two fetched schematic revisions (v1.11, v1.12) agree on every net named below.

power.name: 5V in (USB-C OTG)
power.cite: [brief] §5.1 p.5 verbatim: 'The Radxa ZERO 3W support DC +5V voltage: Power adapter with 5V/2A on the USB 2.0 OTG Type‑C power port'. [wiki] 'USB C': 'There are two USB TYPE-C ports, one is USB 2.0 OTG port and the other is USB3.0 HOST port. The power supply is USB 2.0 OTG port.' [sch1.12] sheet 22 'Power_DC IN': J2 USB_TYPEC_115H0, VBUS_1..4 → FB120/3A → VCC_SYS; CC1/CC2 through R9/R10 5.1k (the sink-side Rd on the OTG port itself).

power.name: 5V in (40-pin)
power.cite: [brief] §5.1 p.5 verbatim: '5V Power from the GPIO PIN 2 & 4'. This is the path docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §9 infers for the HAT ('battery → banana contact PCB → HAT → 40-pin (5 V to Radxa)'); the HAT's regulator is CANNOT DETERMINE.

power.name: USB3 host port current
power.cite: [brief] §6.2 p.6: 'a USB 3.0 Host Type‑C interface, constrained to a maximum electrical current of 500mA in accordance with USB 3.0 specifications'. [sch1.12] sheet 17: SY6280AAC load switch feeding AO_5V_B on the host port.

power.name: PMIC
power.cite: [sch1.12] sheet 21 'Power_PMIC': 'RK817-5' (PMIC + codec, I2C0, BUCK1–4, LDO1–9); sheet 22: RK860-0 for VDD_CPU. Board-level current draw: NOT stated in any fetched document — CANNOT DETERMINE.

header_40pin.$about: Pin → function, read off [brief] §6.1.1 p.6 'GPIO Alternate Functions' table (text layer) and cross-checked against [wiki] '40 PIN GPIO' table. Only the pins the Microduck uses or a HAT designer must know are listed; both sources carry the full 40.
header_40pin.pullups_note: [wiki] tip verbatim: 'Pin 3, Pin 5, Pin 27, and Pin 28 add extra pull-up resistors for I2C device power supply, so they work abnormally when used as GPIOs.' — the board ALREADY pulls I2C3_M0 up; the HAT's R12/R13 10 kΩ (docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §11) are in parallel with them. The on-board value: not printed on the wiki; [sch1.12] sheet 20 'CONNECTOR' was not read for it — CANNOT DETERMINE.
header_40pin.verdict_why: two independent vendor pages agree on every listed pin (brief p.6 table and wiki table, both read 2026-09-02).

buses_the_microduck_uses.servo_bus_uart2_m0: SETTLES docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md open question 10 (UART2 header pins). [wiki] 'Debug Serial Port' verbatim: 'The debug serial port of ZERO 3 uses UART2_M0 (40-pin GPIO Pin 8: TX, Pin 10: RX), with a default baud rate of 1500000n8.' and 'UART2_M0 is also the default U-Boot console. If you enable UART2_M0 as a normal serial port through the rsetup overlay, input on the serial port will interrupt the boot process and the device may fail to boot.' [sch1.12] sheet 6 'RK3566_OSC/PLL/PMUIO' (sheet numbers = PDF pages = the title block's 'Sheet N of 22'): UART2_TX_M0 / GPIO0_D1_u and UART2_RX_M0 / GPIO0_D0_u. So the Dynamixel bus (/dev/ttyS2, robotd.toml [bus]) is on header pins 8 (TX) / 10 (RX) at 3.3 V — and it is the U-Boot console, which is exactly why Pollen masks serial-getty@ttyS2 (rdesign:58-61). Whether U-Boot's console output at 1.5 Mbaud reaches the servos at boot: CANNOT DETERMINE (the wiki's warning is about INPUT interrupting boot).
buses_the_microduck_uses.i2c3_m0_pins_3_5: [brief] p.6 table: pin 3 'I2C3_SDA_M0 | UART3_RX_M0 | GPIO1_A0', pin 5 'I2C3_SCL_M0 | UART3_TX_M0 | GPIO1_A1'. Agrees with Pollen's overlay (GPIO1_A0 SDA / GPIO1_A1 SCL, docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md §11). [sch1.12] sheet 12 'RK3566_Audio Interface' shows the M0 alternates 'I2C3_SDA_M0 / UART3_RX_M0 / … / GPIO1_A0_u' and 'I2C3_SCL_M0 / UART3_TX_M0 / … / GPIO1_A1_u'; sheet 11 'RK3566_VO Interface_2' shows the M1 alternates 'I2C3_SCL_M1 … GPIO3_B5_d' and 'I2C3_SDA_M1 … GPIO3_B6_d', whose nets go to the Type-C controller U6 on sheet 17 — which is why the overlay re-muxes I2C3 to M0 and disables the 'fusb302@22' node (part:et7301b).
buses_the_microduck_uses.i2s3_m0: [brief] p.6 / [wiki]: I2S3_SCLK_M0 pin 12 (GPIO3_A3), I2S3_MCLK_M0 pin 13 (GPIO3_A2), I2S3_LRCK_M0 pin 35 (GPIO3_A4), I2S3_SDI_M0 pin 38 (GPIO3_A6), I2S3_SDO_M0 pin 40 (GPIO3_A5). SETTLES the I2S half of open question 10 for the M0 mux; Pollen's aic.dts uses 'i2s3_2ch' — whether it selects the M0 pins (header) or M1 (pins 19/21/23/24, also on the header) was not read from the dts here: CANNOT DETERMINE which mux, both are on the 40-pin. MCLK: I2S3_MCLK_M0 on pin 13 is a candidate origin for the overlay's 12 MHz 'fixed-clock' (docs §7) — consistent, not proven.
buses_the_microduck_uses.mipi_csi: [wiki] 'MIPI CSI' table, 22 pins: 1 GND, 2 MIPI_CSI_RX_D0N, 3 D0P, 4 GND, 5 D1N, 6 D1P, 7 GND, 8 CLK0N, 9 CLK0P, 10 GND, 11 D2N, 12 D2P, 13 GND, 14 D3N, 15 D3P, 16 GND, 17 CAMERAB_PDN_L, 18 CIF_CLKOUT, 19 GND, 20 I2C2_SCL_M1, 21 I2C2_SDA_M1, 22 VCC_3V3. [product]: '22-Pin MIPI CSI with 0.5mm Pitch'. [brief] §6.3 p.7: '1x4‑lane MIPI CSI'. [sch1.12] sheet 9 'RK3566_VI Interface': J7, 4 lanes (MIPI_CSI_RX_D0..D3, CLK0), I2C2_SCL_M1/SDA_M1, CAMERAB_PDN_L on the GPIO3_C6_d line. Pollen's probe 'imx219 2-0010' = I2C bus 2, address 0x10 (part:imx219) — matches I2C2.
buses_the_microduck_uses.usb_c_pd_controller: [sch1.12] sheet 17 'USB Port': U6 'ET7301B' at J9 'USB_TYPEC_115H0' (the USB3 HOST port), VDD on VCC_3V3, SCL/SDA on I2C3_SCL_M1/I2C3_SDA_M1, INT# → TYPEC_INT (GPIO on sheet 9). [sch1.11] sheet 17: same part. The OTG/power port J2 (sheet 22) has NO controller — 5.1 kΩ Rd on CC1/CC2 (R9/R10), so it is a plain 5 V sink. Pollen's 'fusb302@22' node is this U6, disabled by the overlay.

record.thermal: [brief] §6.5 p.7 verbatim: 'The specified ambient operating temperature for optimal performance of the Radxa ZERO 3W ranges from 0°C to 50°C'; 'An internal thermal management governor is in place to regulate these parameters, ensuring that the CPU temperature does not exceed a threshold of 85°C.' (Pollen's media notes: flat-out 95 °C and throttling to 408 MHz — docs §2 — sits above the brief's 85 °C governor claim; recorded as a disagreement between vendor prose and Pollen's measurement.)
